title_en: The importance of the Arabic language
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فإن من لطف الله تعالى ونعمه ورحمته أن جعل للناس لسانا يتفاهمون به، فالناس يحتاج بعضهم لبعض ولا يمكن أن يقوم أحد منهم بحاجته دون بعض، ولا يمكن أن يستقل منهم إنسان بقضاء أموره ولا بأداء مهماته إلا إذا وجد من يساعده على ذلك، ومن هنا احتاجوا إلى التفاهم فيما بينهم والتعارف، فجعل الله لهم وسائل للتعارف ومن أعظمها الأنساب حيث قال تعالى: {يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَائِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوا إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ} وجعل لهم وسائل للتفاهم وأعظمها اللغات ولهذا ربط الله بين الألوان واللغات وبين خلق السماوات والأرض في قوله تعالى: {وَمِنْ آَيَاتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافُ أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَأَلْوَانِكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآَيَاتٍ لِلْعَالِمِينَ} فالبشر لا يمكن أن يتفاهموا إلا عن طريق وسائل الحس، إلا عن طريق الحواس الخمس، لأن وسائل العلم لدى الإنسان ثلاث، هي العقل والروح والحس..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: it is among God Most High's kindness and His favours and His mercy that He made for people a tongue by which they understand one another. People have need of one another, and none of them can meet his need without others; none of them can be independent in managing his affairs or in discharging his tasks unless he finds someone to help him in that. From this they had need to understand one another and to know one another. So God made for them means of knowing one another, the greatest of which are lineages, as God Most High said: {O mankind, We have created you from a male and a female, and made you peoples and tribes, that you may know one another. Indeed the most honoured of you with God is the most God-conscious of you} (Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt 49:13). And He made for them means of understanding one another, the greatest of which are languages. For this reason God linked colours and languages with the creation of the heavens and the earth, in His words, Most High: {And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your tongues and your colours. Indeed in that are signs for those who know} (Sūrat al-Rūm 30:22). Human beings cannot understand one another except by way of the means of sense — except by way of the five senses — because the means of knowledge a person has are three: the intellect, the spirit and the senses..

flags.arabic: لأن وسائل العلم لدى الإنسان ثلاث، هي العقل والروح والحس
flags.context: the closing sentence of the published excerpt
options: the intellect, the spirit and the senses
the mind, the soul and the senses
flags.note: This threefold division of the means of knowledge is a substantive epistemological claim and the excerpt ends before the Sheikh unfolds it, so the intended weight of each of the three terms cannot be settled from this text. Rūḥ is rendered 'the spirit' rather than 'the soul' to keep it distinct from nafs, which is separately rendered elsewhere in this slice. A reviewer should check the rendering against the Sheikh's fuller treatments of the same division before it is fixed for the corpus.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
The record is a lecture transcript, not a written essay: it opens with the spoken doxology and the greeting to the audience, and it is typed 'transcript' for that reason.

The Sheikh's argument moves from the need for cooperation, to the need for mutual recognition, to language as the means of it. The chain has been preserved as a chain rather than compressed into the title's assertion about the importance of Arabic — which the excerpt does not in fact reach.
The verse references have been supplied per house style; the source gives the verse texts alone, vocalised, with the brace brackets it uses for Qur'anic quotation.

'Those who know' renders al-ʿālimīn at Sūrat al-Rūm 30:22. The reading printed in the source is al-ʿālimīn ('those who know'), not al-ʿālamīn ('the worlds'); the two differ by a single vowel and the source's vocalisation has been followed.
